description: A graduate course on turning data into decisions: decision analysis under uncertainty, predictive models, optimisation, simulation, experiments and causal inference, applied to operations and marketing. Students query business data in SQL, build and evaluate models, run simulations and finish with a recommendation to a decision maker.
modelledOn: Davenport and Harris, Competing on Analytics
Provost and Fawcett, Data Science for Business
Winston, Operations Research: Applications and Algorithms
Kohavi, Tang and Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments
outcomes: Structure a business decision under uncertainty and compute expected value, the value of information and the effect of risk attitude.
Build, evaluate and compare predictive models for demand, churn and credit risk using cost-aware metrics.
Formulate and solve linear, integer and simulation models of operations problems and interpret shadow prices and risk.
Design, analyse and critique experiments and observational studies to estimate causal effects.
Apply analytics to pricing, inventory, segmentation and marketing allocation problems.
Deliver an end-to-end analytics project with a clear recommendation, a business case and an honest account of limits and ethics.

units.title: Decision analysis under uncertainty
topics: Descriptive, predictive and prescriptive analytics; the analytics value chain
Decision trees, expected monetary value and the expected value of perfect information
Utility theory, risk attitude and certainty equivalents
Bayesian updating of beliefs and the expected value of sample information
Sensitivity analysis and tornado diagrams for decision models

units.title: Predictive modelling for business
topics: Linear, ridge and lasso regression for demand forecasting
Logistic regression for churn and credit default; ROC, AUC and calibration
Tree ensembles: random forests, gradient boosting and feature importance
Time series forecasting: decomposition, exponential smoothing, ARIMA and forecast error (MAPE)
Cost-sensitive evaluation: profit curves, lift charts and threshold choice
Model risk: leakage, drift and fairness in lending decisions

units.title: Optimisation and simulation
topics: Linear programming formulations: product mix, blending and transportation; the simplex method
Sensitivity analysis, shadow prices and reduced costs
Integer and binary programming: knapsack, facility location and branch and bound
Monte Carlo simulation of business processes and distribution fitting
Discrete-event simulation of queues in banks and call centres
Optimisation under uncertainty: the newsvendor problem and simple stochastic programs

units.title: Experimentation and causal inference
topics: Potential outcomes, confounding and causal diagrams
A/B tests: hypothesis testing, power, sample size and multiple comparisons
Sequential testing and multi-armed bandits with Thompson sampling
Observational methods: matching, propensity scores and difference-in-differences
Uplift modelling and heterogeneous treatment effects
Threats to validity: Simpson's paradox, selection bias, interference and the ethics of experiments

units.title: Analytics in operations and marketing
topics: Customer segmentation: RFM analysis and k-means clustering
Customer lifetime value and churn timing with survival analysis
Pricing and revenue management: price elasticity, markdown optimisation and overbooking
Inventory models: economic order quantity, safety stock and reorder points
Delivery routing heuristics and demand-driven supply chain planning for last-mile logistics
Marketing mix modelling, attribution and budget allocation

units.title: The analytics project lifecycle
topics: Framing the business problem, success metrics and the CRISP-DM cycle
Data readiness and feature engineering in SQL at scale
Deployment, monitoring and model decay
Governance, privacy and responsible analytics under data protection law
The business case for analytics: return on investment and the cost of wrong predictions

units.title: Communicating analytical results
topics: Data storytelling: audience, question, answer and next step
Visual design for decisions: chart choice and showing uncertainty
Dashboards and KPI design: pitfalls of proxy metrics
Writing the executive memo and defending a recommendation

units.title: Capstone analytics project
topics: Scoping a project and auditing the data
An integrated pipeline: predict, optimise and test
Critique and defence of results before a panel
Reflection on limits, bias and operational follow-through

schedule.title: Decision trees and the analytics value chain
schedule.exercise: Build a decision tree for a retailer choosing between opening a shop in Kumasi or Tamale or waiting, compute expected value and the value of perfect information.

tasks.title: Roll back a given two-stage decision tree with probabilities and payoffs, and report the best strategy and its expected monetary value
Compute the expected value of perfect information for a promotion decision and state the most one would pay for a market survey
Write SQL on a sales table that produces descriptive, trend and segment summaries, and note which prescriptive question each one leaves open

schedule.title: Risk, Bayes and sensitivity
schedule.exercise: Compute the certainty equivalent for a risk-averse owner, update a belief about a new product with a pilot sale, and draw a tornado chart of the key inputs.

tasks.title: Fit an exponential utility to three lottery choices and compute the certainty equivalent for a risky investment
Update the probability that demand is high after a pilot of 20 customers using Bayes rule and report the revised decision
Vary each input of a profit model over its range, plot a tornado chart and name the two inputs worth more data collection

schedule.title: Regression, classification and ensembles
schedule.exercise: Predict weekly demand with a regularised regression and predict loan default with logistic regression and a boosted tree, and compare AUC on held-out data.

tasks.title: Fit ridge and lasso regression on a retail sales dataset, choose the penalty by cross-validation and report the held-out error
Train a logistic regression for mobile loan default, plot the ROC curve, and report AUC and calibration in ten bins
Train a random forest and a boosted tree on the same data, tune each with a grid search, and compare importance rankings

schedule.title: Forecasting, cost-sensitive evaluation and model risk
schedule.exercise: Forecast four weeks of sales with exponential smoothing and ARIMA, choose a classification threshold using a profit curve, and check a model for leakage.

tasks.title: Forecast 8 weeks of daily sales with exponential smoothing and ARIMA, and compare MAPE on a held-out final month
Plot a profit curve using a cost matrix for false positives and negatives and choose the threshold that maximises profit
Find the leaked feature in a given churn model, retrain without it, and compare error rates across gender and region groups

schedule.title: Linear and integer programming
schedule.exercise: Formulate a product mix for a small food factory as a linear program, read the shadow prices, then add integer batch sizes and compare the solutions.

tasks.title: Solve a two-product mix problem graphically, mark the feasible region and the optimal vertex, and report profit at the vertex
Solve a transportation problem from three depots to four markets and interpret the shadow price on each capacity constraint
Solve a facility-location problem for six candidate clinics as a binary program and compare with the linear relaxation bound

schedule.title: Simulation of business systems
schedule.exercise: Simulate a bank with three tellers to find the staffing that keeps the 90th percentile wait under 5 minutes, and solve a newsvendor problem for daily bread stock.

tasks.title: Simulate 10000 trials of the profit of a new product with uncertain price and cost and report the probability of a loss
Write a discrete-event simulation of one queue with random arrivals and service, and report mean wait for 1, 2 and 3 servers
Find the order quantity for a perishable product that maximises expected profit using the critical ratio, and confirm it by simulation

schedule.title: Causal questions and A/B tests
schedule.exercise: Design an A/B test for a new checkout screen: choose the metric, compute the sample size and run a bandit alternative on simulated traffic.

tasks.title: Draw a causal diagram for the effect of a discount on repeat purchases, marking a confounder and a collider, and say which to adjust for
Compute the sample size for a 2 percent lift in conversion at 80 percent power, then analyse a simulated test and report the confidence interval
Run Thompson sampling against a fixed split on three ad variants for 5000 impressions and compare cumulative conversions

schedule.title: Observational causal methods and uplift
schedule.exercise: Estimate the effect of a loyalty programme from observational data with matching and difference-in-differences, and explain how Simpson's paradox could reverse the naive answer.

tasks.title: Estimate a propensity score for a loyalty programme, match customers, and compare the treatment effect with the naive difference
Build a table where a treatment looks harmful overall but helpful in every subgroup, and explain the reversal with weighted rates
Fit an uplift model on a simulated coupon experiment, rank customers by predicted uplift, and compute the Qini curve gain

schedule.title: Segmentation, lifetime value and pricing
schedule.exercise: Segment customers of a telecom by recency, frequency and value, estimate lifetime value per segment, and set a markdown schedule for seasonal stock.

tasks.title: Compute recency, frequency and monetary value per customer in SQL from a transactions table and bucket customers into quintiles
Cluster customers with k-means for k from 2 to 8, choose k with a silhouette score and describe each segment in business terms
Estimate price elasticity from sales history and compute the markdown path that clears stock in 8 weeks at maximum revenue

schedule.title: Inventory, routing and marketing allocation
schedule.exercise: Compute the order quantity and safety stock for a pharmacy item, plan routes for six delivery stops with a heuristic, and split an advertising budget across channels.

tasks.title: Compute EOQ, reorder point and safety stock for demand of 40 units a day with 5 day lead time at a 95 percent service level
Build a delivery route for 12 stops with a nearest-neighbour heuristic and improve it with 2-opt, reporting the distance saved
Fit a marketing mix regression on weekly spend by channel and choose the budget split that maximises predicted sales under a cap

schedule.title: The analytics project lifecycle
schedule.exercise: Write a project charter for a churn-reduction project with metrics, data needs, deployment plan, privacy risks and a cost-benefit estimate.

tasks.title: Engineer 10 customer features in SQL with window functions and check a query plan to make the feature table build under a time limit
Compute the net value of a churn model from its confusion matrix, intervention cost and customer value at three thresholds
Respond as the analytics lead in a scenario where marketing wants to use personal location data, scored on consent, minimisation and value

schedule.title: Communicating results
schedule.exercise: Turn a modelling result into a one-page executive memo with one chart, one recommendation and the main risk, and present it in three minutes.

tasks.title: Redraw a cluttered chart as a clear one with a single message title, direct labels and an uncertainty band, and justify each change
Define five KPIs for a delivery service with SQL for each, and note how each could be gamed by staff
Present a forecast with an interval to a sceptical board in a scenario and answer rounds of questions, scored on clarity and honesty about limits

schedule.title: Capstone: predict, optimise, test
schedule.exercise: Complete and defend an end-to-end project on a supplied business dataset: a model, an optimisation, a test plan and a recommendation, with limits stated.

tasks.title: Audit a business dataset in SQL for missing values, duplicates and impossible values and report a data quality score for each table
Build a pipeline that forecasts demand, feeds the forecast into an inventory optimisation and reports the expected cost saving with a range
Defend your recommendation in a scenario panel that questions assumptions, bias and operational follow-through, scored on rigour and candour
